claim: The C# 14 `field` keyword can be used to implement lazy initialization in a property setter without declaring a private field.
note: Passage puts lazy initialization in the getter; setter scenarios are constraints and change notification.

claim: While runtime improvements like JIT inlining and stack allocations benefit existing code, specific application-level bottlenecks will always require manual optimization using best practices like minimizing exceptions or avoiding blocking calls.
note: Passage gives guidelines; never says bottlenecks always require manual optimization.

claim: ASP.NET Core 10.0 introduces passkey support for Identity, built on the WebAuthn standard.
note: Passage lists passkey support for Identity; WebAuthn is never mentioned.

claim: C# 14 introduces field-backed properties and partial methods.
note: 'complementing partial methods and properties introduced in C# 13'.

claim: A new property in the .NET 10 SDK allows users to explicitly set the format of tab-completion scripts.
note: The new property sets the format of container images; the CLI merely generates native tab-completion scripts.

claim: "ASP.NET Core Identity is related to the Microsoft identity platform".
note: 'ASP.NET Core Identity isn't related to the Microsoft identity platform.'

claim: C# 14 introduces field-backed properties, which replace auto-implemented properties.
note: Passage: they 'provide a smoother path from auto-implemented properties'; nothing says they replace them.

claim: .NET 10 is a long-term support (LTS) release, supported for two years.
note: 'is supported for three years as a long-term support (LTS) release'.

claim: C# 14 introduces first-class support for implicit conversions of `Span<T>` and `ReadOnlySpan<T>`, which are stack-only ref struct types.
note: Passage lists the conversion feature only; it never describes spans as stack-only ref structs.

claim: A new property in the .NET 10 SDK lets you explicitly set the format of container images, so console apps can now natively create them.
note: Both facts stated side by side; no causal link between the format property and native container creation.

claim: The `nameof` expression in C# 14 supports unbound generic types like `List<>`, but still requires a type argument.
note: 'returns the name of the type without requiring a type argument'.

claim: In EF Core 10, the SQL sent to the database shows the redacted version: `IN (?, ?)`.
note: 'EF10 sends the same SQL to the database, but logs the following SQL, where the roles have been redacted'.

claim: Field-backed properties allow accessing the compiler-generated backing field using the value contextual keyword.
note: Passage names `field` as the keyword denoting the backing field; `value` is never said to access it.

claim: The feature allows strings to be passed directly to APIs expecting `ReadOnlySpan<char>`, which has been possible since C# 7.2.
note: Spans arrived in C# 7.2, but 'In the past, you had to call .AsSpan() on a string'; implicit conversion is new in C# 14.

claim: "Optimizations in .NET and ASP.NET Core mean that newer versions generally outperform older versions"; for example, ASP.NET Core 2.1 added support for HTTP/2.
note: 'ASP.NET Core 2.2 added support for HTTP/2'; 2.1 is cited for compiled regular expressions and Span<T>.

claim: C# 14 introduces first-class support for implicit conversions of `Span<T>` and `ReadOnlySpan<T>`, which is why Visual Basic now prefers Span-based overloads.
note: VB prefers Span-based overloads because it respects OverloadResolutionPriorityAttribute; no link to C# 14 conversions stated.

claim: ASP.NET Core 10.0 introduces automatic memory pool eviction for Blazor WebAssembly apps only.
note: Memory pool eviction is listed without any Blazor WebAssembly restriction; preloading is the WebAssembly item.

claim: F# 10 introduces "First-class support for implicit conversions of `Span<T>` and `ReadOnlySpan<T>`".
note: The span conversion bullet sits under C# 14; the F# section lists other changes.

claim: This posed no risk of leaking sensitive data like role names or user identifiers into log files.
note: 'the potentially sensitive values were logged'; redaction 'prevents that information from leaking into the application logs'.

claim: EF Core has the ability to redact inlined constants from logging by default on all database providers.
note: Passage never states provider coverage for redaction; 'consult your EF provider' refers to JSON updates.

claim: This allows APIs that accept span-based parameters to be called more directly, which is why the BCL has removed its array-based `MemoryExtensions` overloads.
note: Passage says the team 'can now provide a single overload'; it never says existing overloads were removed.

claim: In C# 14, you can access the compiler-generated backing field using the `field` contextual keyword, which can break code that already uses `field` as an identifier.
note: Passage describes the `field` keyword but says nothing about breaking existing identifiers.

claim: "Minimize large object allocations" is a specific piece of advice associated with sourceIndex: 2, as large objects require a generation 1 garbage collection.
note: Large objects 'require a full (generation 2) garbage collection to clean up'.

claim: EF Core 10 can redact inlined constants from logs by default, a change proposed in #32018.
note: #32018 is credited for the non-expression ExecuteUpdateAsync lambda, not log redaction.

claim: When EF Core inlines parameters into SQL statements (for example, when using `EF.Constant()` to improve query plan caching), those values were previously redacted from logs.
note: 'in those scenarios, the potentially sensitive values were logged. EF10 no longer does this'.
